summary: Mitchell County lookout on Woody's Knob, Little Switzerland, reportedly built 1958; a 1958-60 biennial report dates a tower cabin. Current status not found.

facts.agency: North Carolina Division of Forest Resources
facts.status_note: No source found says whether the tower still stands.

events.note: Per a Facebook group post, the lookout and fire tower on Woody's Knob in Little Switzerland was constructed in 1958. The post is user-generated and unverified.
Tower cabin (not the tower itself), per a biennial report covering 1958-60, which gives no single year.

notes_for_editor: The cached Facebook page holds only its first line, so the 1958 date rests on a user-generated post. Its fuller text was seen only in a search snippet that is not in the cache, so it is not quoted. That snippet appears to describe later history (a 1980s state closure, a last observer from 1979 to 1988, remaining buildings, a 68.9-foot height). Check the post by hand before using any of it. The post dates the tower to 1958 and the report gives 1958-60 for the cabin; the span is consistent with 1958 but does not confirm it. The story's earlier claim that the tower was built 'to help detect woodland fires' was removed on 2026-10-21 because the cached post text does not contain that purpose. The brief places the record in Spruce Pine town, but the post says Woody's Knob in Little Switzerland. Check the brief coordinates (35.87972, -82.10444) against that. Not on the NHLR North Carolina list or the FFLOS North Carolina list.
